purpose: Public recordings analyzed for timbre and timing; generated candidates contain no reference audio.

references.title: Tornado siren in Streamwood IL.wav
references.author: audible-edge
references.measurement: Public 56-second preview, mono decode at 48 kHz: prominent sustained components around 468-470 and 702-704 Hz during 5-20 seconds, higher harmonics and later pitch coast-down.
references.limitation: Author describes editing/filtering/compression of a close test recording. Recorded ratios do not establish a particular siren model or unprocessed source response.

references.title: Thunderbolt 1000T In Alert (Ambience
references.author: mordeby
references.measurement: Public 79.993-second preview: sustained components around 600 and 720 Hz at 20-30 seconds, startup pitch rise and time-varying level; substantial environmental low-frequency noise.
references.limitation: Model and recording location are supplied by the uploader. Ambient noise and propagation prevent treating the recorded amplitudes as factory calibration.

references.finding: Manufacturer describes rotor/stator air pulses, pitch tied to motor speed, steady and wailing signals, and a 533 Hz top frequency for the 60 Hz version (printed pages 7, 9-10).

Manufacturer describes a directional projector rotating at 3 RPM (20 seconds/revolution), with steady, wail and fast-wail options. A slow amplitude swell is a design approximation, not a faithful model of propagation.

distribution: Only original synth outputs are audition masters. Reference recordings stay in ignored analysis artifacts and are not copied into Content, cooked packages or generated sounds.
